 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT In this appeal, the petitioner/appellant has challenged the judgment and award dated 16.03.2013 passed in M.V.C.No.123/2012 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura ('the Tribunal' for short). 
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal. 
3. Brief facts of the case are, on 09.09.2011 at about 3.15 p.m., while the petitioner was standing on the left side of the road on NH-17, Kundapura along with his mother, Motor Cycle bearing Regn.
No.KA-47-J-0900 dashed against him, causing him injuries. He was treated at Govt. Hospital Bhatkal and R.N.S. Hospital, Murdeshwara under hospitalization. The petitioner being a minor through his NC: 2024:KHC:30741 guardian mother approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation. Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company. After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by the impugned judgment, assessed compensation of Rs.90,700/-, attributed 50% contributory negligence against the petitioner, and awarded 50% of the compensation i.e., Rs.45,350/- with interest @ 6% per annum. Aggrieved by the same and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds. 
4. Heard the arguments of Sri.Nagaraja Hegde, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.K.N.Srinivasa, learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was aged six years. 
After alighting from the Auto Rickshaw, he was standing along with his mother on the left side of the road. Ex.P3 mahazar explained that the place of accident is extreme left side of the road. The petitioner and his mother were not crossing the road but the Tribunal has erroneously misinterpreted the NC: 2024:KHC:30741 admission of the mother of the petitioner in the cross-examination, who is an illiterate lady, without knowing consequences given such a statement. 
Ex.P2 complaint, filed by an eye witness, who specifically stated that the place of accident is left side of the road. When the material on record explained that the accident was on the left side of the road,
it is not a case of road crossing and thereby the contributory negligence attributing 50% against the Mr Master Samar Ali vs Mr Abdul Salam on 2 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187277059/
2 petitioner needs to be removed. 
5.1. It is further contended that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both the bones of the left leg,
fracture of left humorous and he was under hospitalization for 16 days. He was attended by his mother for more than six months. The compensation assessed by the tribunal on the meager side is without applying the principle for assessing the compensation in the case of this nature. As regarding disability is concerned, the learned counsel relied upon the judgment of MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396.
NC: 2024:KHC:30741 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner and his mother were alighted from the Auto Rickshaw on the NH-17, Kundapura. National Highway is meant for fast moving of the vehicle. It is the duty of the parents to take care of the minor child while crossing the road. The petitioner was crossing the road along with his mother has admitted by the mother herself in the course of cross-examination and for this reason Tribunal has rightly attributed 50% contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner. The petitioner no doubt suffered the injuries, but the compensation assessed is proportionate to the injuries sustained. The medical expenses have been reimbursed by the Tribunal and he has supported the impugned judgment. 
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both parties and perused the materials on record. 
8. The prosecution papers on record goes to point out that there was an accident on 19.09.2011 at 3.15 p.m. The petitioner along with his mother came to the spot of the NC: 2024:KHC:30741 accident in Auto Rickshaw at NH-17 and has alighted at the spot. They were intended to go to a mall situated on the other side of the road. At that time, Motor Cycle bearing Regn. No.KA-47-J-0900 hit against the petitioner causing him injuries. Medical records show that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both bones of the left leg and fracture of left humorous. He was under hospitalization for 16 days. 
9. During the course of cross-examination, the mother of the petitioner has admitted that there was no fault on the part of the rider of the Motor Cycle. Such evidence cannot be accepted even for logical purpose as it is the duty of the rider of the motor vehicle to take care of the road safety of the pedestrians who are crossing the road. The mahazar at Ex.P3 and complaint Ex. P2 clearly point out that the place of the accident is not the middle of the road and it was on the extreme left side of the road. Even taking into consideration that the petitioner has crossed the road, the attribution of 50%
contributory negligence cannot be supported with. As a pedestrian, it is a duty of the mother to take care of the child. For the negligence of the parents it is NC: 2024:KHC:30741 proper to attribute negligence to an extent of 25% on that of the Motor Cycle at 75 % and accordingly, the compensation has to be awarded. 
Mr Master Samar Ali vs Mr Abdul Salam on 2 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187277059/
3 10. As regarding injuries and the treatment, the petitioner has relied on the evidence of PW-3, the treated doctor, who has spoken about the treatment as well as 15% whole body disability sustained by the petitioner. The medical evidence is persuasive and the whole body disability sustained by the petitioner could be taken as 15%. Insofar as the assessment of loss of future income on account of disability, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mallikarjun (supra) at para 12 held that it will be a difficult task to make accurate assessment of compensation when the child suffering disability on account of motor vehicle accident. Hon'ble Apex Court held that it is desirable to award compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- in case of disability up to 30%, Rs.4,00,000/- up to 60%,
Rs.5,00,000/- up to 90% and Rs.6,00,000/- in case of 100%. In that case, Hon'ble Apex Court held that Rs.1,00,000/- shall be compensated in case the permanent disability is up to 10%. Having regard to NC: 2024:KHC:30741 the 15% of the whole body disability, it is just and proper to assess Rs.1,50,000/- as a compensation towards disability suffered by the petitioner. 
11. The petitioner has suffered fractures, undergone pain and sufferings and loss of amenities and discomfort. Hence, towards pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/- and towards loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.50,000/- is assessed. Medical bills of Rs.39,700/- is to be reimbursed. Towards incidental expenses such as attendant charges, travel expenses and food and nourishment a sum of Rs.10,000/- is assessed. The petitioner laid up minimum of three months for the nature of injuries and has to be attended by his mother, loss of income during the laid up of the child will be Rs.19,500/-(Rs.6,500/- x 3). The child required future treatment and a sum of Rs.10,000/- is assessed towards future medical expenses. 
12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
NC: 2024:KHC:30741 Particulars Amount 1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs. 39,700/-
3. Loss of income during laid Rs. 19,500/-
up period 4. Loss of future income Rs. 1,50,000/-
5. Loss of amenities and Rs. 50,000/-
discomfort 6. Attendant charges, food Rs. 10,000/- & nourishment and transportation 7. Future medical expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 Total Rs. 3,29,200/-
Mr Master Samar Ali vs Mr Abdul Salam on 2 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187277059/
4  13. Thereby the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,29,200/-. It is just and proper compensation that the petitioner is entitled under the facts and circumstances of the case. 
14. In view of the discussion supra, 25% of the compensation has to be deducted towards negligence of the part of the parents. Thereby the petitioner is entitled to 75% of the compensation, which comes to Rs.2,46,900/-. 
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:30741 15. Liability on the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured is not in dispute. Hence,
the appeal merits consideration, in result, the following: 
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part;
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified;
(iii) The petitioner would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,46,900/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation;
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said compensation with interest @ 6% per annum excluding interest on future medical expenses (i.e.,
Rs.7,500/-). 
(v) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount along with accrued interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment. 
SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE ABK Mr Master Samar Ali vs Mr Abdul Salam on 2 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187277059/

The child required future treatment and a sum of Rs.10,000/- is assessed towards future medical expenses.
12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

2. Medical Expenses Rs. 39,700/-
3. Loss of income during laid Rs. 19,500/-
up period 4. Loss of future income Rs. 1,50,000/-
5. Loss of amenities and Rs. 50,000/-
discomfort 6.
Attendant charges, food Rs. 10,000/- & nourishment and transportation 7.
Thereby the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,29,200/-.
14. In view of the discussion supra, 25% of the compensation has to be deducted towards negligence of the part of the parents.
Thereby the petitioner is entitled to 75% of the compensation, which comes to Rs.2,46,900/-.
Liability on the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured is not in dispute.
Hence,
the appeal merits consideration, in result, the following:

ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part;
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified;
(iii) The petitioner would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,46,900/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation;
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said compensation with interest @ 6% per annum excluding interest on future medical expenses (i.e.,
Rs.7,500/-).

(v) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount along with accrued interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
